ANABOHUN.name: Anne of Bohemia and Hungary
ANABOHUN.summary: Consort of the Jagiellon dynasty. Their life was connected with Austria, Bohemia and Hungary.

MARIAJOSEPHAAUSTRIASAX.name: Maria Josepha of Austria
MARIAJOSEPHAAUSTRIASAX.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life was connected with Austria, Saxony and Poland.

MARIAAMALIAHAB1701.name: Maria Amalia of Austria
MARIAAMALIAHAB1701.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life was connected with Bavaria, Holy Roman Empire and Austria.

GUGL9MON.name: William IX of Montferrat
GUGL9MON.summary: He inherited Montferrat from Boniface III and married Anne of Alençon. His children Margaret and Boniface would occupy different positions in the succession: Boniface inherited the marquisate, while Margaret transmitted the rights that would eventually support its incorporation into the Gonzaga inheritance.
GUGL9MON.biography: He inherited Montferrat from Boniface III and married Anne of Alençon. His children Margaret and Boniface would occupy different positions in the succession: Boniface inherited the marquisate, while Margaret transmitted the rights that would eventually support its incorporation into the Gonzaga inheritance. William’s French marriage strengthened the house’s international connections.

LUIS2FLA.name: Louis II of Flanders
LUIS2FLA.summary: Louis of Male, Count of Flanders since 1346. In the face of the Flemish cities, his daughter Margaret took Flanders to the dukes of Burgundy.

LEONAUST.name: Eleanor of Austria
LEONAUST.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life was connected with Portugal, France and Austria.

ISABCLARAEUG.name: Isabella Clara Eugenia
ISABCLARAEUG.summary: She exercised the sovereignty over the Low Countries with Albert and then continued as governor. Her political role was much broader than that of a dynastic consort.

governmentNotes.Autoridad compartida; no se interpreta c: Shared authority; not interpreted as exclusive succession.
governmentNotes.Gobernadora de Felipe IV después de la m: Governor of Philip IV after the death of Albert and the reversal of sovereignty in 1621; the office does not transmit the king's provincial titles to him.
governmentNotes.Soberanía compartida por Alberto e Isabe: Sovereignty shared by Albert and Isabella Clara Eugenia after the cession of Philip II; subject to the outcome of the war in each territory.

JACOBA.name: Jacqueline of Bavaria
JACOBA.summary: She inherited Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland from her father and defended her rights against John of Bavaria and Philip the Good. Her marriages formed part of that political struggle. The Agreement of Delft in 1428 restricted her power, and the cession of 1433 incorporated the counties into the Burgundian inheritance.

governmentNotes.Derechos disputados; el acuerdo de Delft: Rights disputed; the Delft agreement of 1428 restricted his government.
governmentNotes.Título conservado bajo la tutela de Feli: Title preserved under the guardianship of Philip the Good until the cession of 1433.

CATANJ.name: Catherine of Anjou
CATANJ.summary: Noble of the Anjou-Hungary dynasty. Their life was connected with Hungary and Silesia.

MARIAANAPORT.name: Maria Anna of Austria
MARIAANAPORT.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life was connected with Portugal and Austria.

JOHN2AVES.name: John II of Avesnes
JOHN2AVES.summary: Count of Hainaut since 1280, inherited Holland and Zeeland in 1299 for his relationship with the Dutch house. The three counties retained their own identities. Their descendants connected them to England, the Wittelsbach and the Bourbons through marriages and successions.

ENRIQUEJOVEN.name: Henry the Young King
ENRIQUEJOVEN.summary: The surviving eldest son of Henry II, was crowned king in his father's life in 1170, but never received effective power. He led the great rebellion of 1173-1174 with his brothers and the support of France, and died in 1183, before his father.

ALB7AUST.name: Albert VII, Archduke of Austria
ALB7AUST.summary: He ruled the Low Countries with Isabella Clara Eugenia. His regime sought to stabilize the Catholic territories and coincided with the Twelve-Year Truce.

governmentNotes.Autoridad compartida; no se interpreta c: Shared authority; not interpreted as exclusive succession.
governmentNotes.Soberanía compartida por Alberto e Isabe: Sovereignty shared by Albert and Isabella Clara Eugenia after the cession of Philip II; subject to the outcome of the war in each territory.

JOHN4TREB.name: John IV of Trebizond
JOHN4TREB.summary: He came to the throne during the rebellion against his father. His government faced the growing Ottoman pressure on the Black Sea routes. Genovese documentation allows his death to be placed in 1460, before David's access.

WILLIAMRICHNASSAU.name: William I of Nassau-Dillenburg
WILLIAMRICHNASSAU.summary: Count of Nassau, 1516–1559. Count of the Nassau dynasty.

HUGH1CYPRUS.name: Hugh I of Cyprus
HUGH1CYPRUS.summary: King of Cyprus since 1205, son of Aimery of Lusignan. He participated in the fifth crusade and died in Tripoli in 1218.

GIANGIACOMOMON.name: John Jacob of Montferrat
GIANGIACOMOMON.summary: A son of Theodore II, he inherited Montferrat and married Joanna of Savoy, sister of Amadeus VIII. Their kinship did not prevent the Savoyard duke from exerting pressure on his lands.
GIANGIACOMOMON.biography: A son of Theodore II, he inherited Montferrat and married Joanna of Savoy, sister of Amadeus VIII. Their kinship did not prevent the Savoyard duke from exerting pressure on his lands. His sons and his daughter Elizabeth connect the later Montferrat succession with the Marquisate of Saluzzo and reveal the links among the three Alpine powers.

JUANRANDAZZO.name: John of Randazzo
JUANRANDAZZO.role: Marquis of Randazzo · Duke of Athens and Neopatras
JUANRANDAZZO.summary: A son of Frederick II of Sicily and Marquis of Randazzo, he inherited the duchies of Athens and Neopatras from his brother William in 1338. Like his brothers, he ruled them from Sicily through vicars until his death in 1348.

GASTON1FOIX.name: Gaston I of Foix
GASTON1FOIX.summary: A son of Roger Bernard III and Margaret of Béarn, he continued the joint inheritance of Foix and Béarn. His sons founded different lines within the family: those of Gaston II and Roger Bernard of Castellbò.
GASTON1FOIX.biography: A son of Roger Bernard III and Margaret of Béarn, he continued the joint inheritance of Foix and Béarn. His sons founded different lines within the family: those of Gaston II and Roger Bernard of Castellbò. The latter line would return to a central position after the extinction of Gaston Fébus’s descendants.

ALBFREDPRUSSIA.name: Albert Frederick of Prussia
ALBFREDPRUSSIA.summary: Duke of Prussia since 1568. His mental illness left the government to his relatives in Brandenburg; his daughter Anna married Juan Segismundo, who inherited Prussia in 1618.

GUIDOFLA.name: Guy of Dampierre
GUIDOFLA.summary: Count of Flanders, 1278–1305. Count of the Dampierre dynasty.

HENRIETTECATHORANGE.name: Henrietta Catherine of Orange-Nassau
HENRIETTECATHORANGE.summary: A daughter of Frederick Henry of Orange and Amalia of Solms, she married John George II of Anhalt-Dessau and served as regent for their son Leopold I from 1693 to 1698.

governmentNotes.Tutela y gobierno del principado durante: Guardianship and government of the principality during the minority of Leopold I; not self-sovereignty over all Anhalt.

KHORASHANKAKH.name: Khorashan of Kartli
KHORASHANKAKH.summary: Daughter of George X of Kartli and wife of Teimuraz I of Kakheti. The marriage strengthened cooperation between the two branches during their wars against Persia. Her children linked this generation to the later kings of Kakheti and Imereti.

JUAN2MONFERRATO.name: John II of Montferrat
JUAN2MONFERRATO.summary: A son of Theodore I, he continued in Montferrat the Palaiologos branch that had arrived from Byzantium. His marriage to Isabella of Majorca added a connection with the Majorcan royal house.
JUAN2MONFERRATO.biography: A son of Theodore I, he continued in Montferrat the Palaiologos branch that had arrived from Byzantium. His marriage to Isabella of Majorca added a connection with the Majorcan royal house. His descendants included Theodore II and Margaret, wife of the Count of Urgell: the same generation illustrates both the Italian line’s continuity and its connections with the Iberian Peninsula.

TEODORO1MON.name: Theodore I of Montferrat
TEODORO1MON.summary: A son of Andronikos II and Irene of Montferrat, he moved from the Byzantine imperial family to the rule of an Italian marquisate. His rights came through his mother, but he had to defend them against rival claimants.
TEODORO1MON.biography: A son of Andronikos II and Irene of Montferrat, he moved from the Byzantine imperial family to the rule of an Italian marquisate. His rights came through his mother, but he had to defend them against rival claimants. Investiture by Henry VII strengthened his position. His children John II and Yolanda connected this new branch with Majorca and Savoy.

VICTORAMADEO1SAB.name: Victor Amadeus I of Savoy
VICTORAMADEO1SAB.summary: Duke of Savoy from 1630 to 1637 and husband of Christine of France, a daughter of Henry IV. Under the Treaty of Cherasco in 1631, he ceded Pinerolo to France.

VIOLHUN.name: Violant of Hungary
VIOLHUN.summary: Consort of the Árpád dynasty. Their life was connected with Aragon.

MARIAAMALIASAJ.name: Maria Amalia of Saxony
MARIAAMALIASAJ.summary: Consort of the Wettin dynasty. Their life was connected with Spain and Saxony.

MARIAJULBERG.name: Maria of Jülich-Berg
MARIAJULBERG.summary: Heiress of the Jülich dynasty. Their life was connected with Jülich, Berg and Cleves.

CONST1GEO.name: Constantine I of Georgia
CONST1GEO.summary: He succeeded his brother George VII. His alliance with Shirvan brought him into conflict with the Qara Qoyunlu; he was captured and executed. Several branches that later contested the Georgian monarchy descended from his children.

BOGISLAW10POM.name: Bogislaw X of Pomerania
BOGISLAW10POM.summary: Duke of Pomerania who gathered under his authority a large part of the territories of the house of the Faucs. His reign strengthened the cohesion of the duchy between Brandenburg, Poland and the Baltic.

JUANARAGURREA.name: Joanna of Aragon and Gurrea
JUANARAGURREA.summary: Consort of the Trastámara dynasty. Their life was connected with Aragon.

ALEX1KAKH.name: Alexander I of Kakheti
ALEX1KAKH.summary: He consolidated the kingdom established by George VIII through flexible diplomacy with the neighbouring powers. He died in a coup led by his son George, an episode that opened another dispute within the royal branch itself.

JACOBO4ESCOCIA.name: James IV of Scotland
JACOBO4ESCOCIA.summary: He strengthened the Scottish court and navy and maintained the alliance with France. He died in Flodden, a defeat that left another regal minority in Scotland.

ISABESLAV.name: Elizabeth of Slavonia
ISABESLAV.summary: Titular consort of the Anjou-Hungary dynasty. Their life was connected with Hungary, Latin Empire and Taranto.

ALBERTPRUSSIA.name: Albert of Prussia
ALBERTPRUSSIA.summary: Last great master of the Teutonic Order in Prussia. In 1525 he secularized his lands as a duchy of Prussia, a vassal of Poland, and adopted Lutheranism; in 1544 he founded the University of Königsberg.

JUAN1BRET.name: John I of Brittany
JUAN1BRET.summary: The son of Alix of Thouars and Peter of Dreux, he inherited the duchy as a child. His father exercised the government during his minority. John's marriage to Blanca de Champagne linked Brittany to the family in Navarre; his son John II continued the ducal line.

JOHANNGEORG2ANHALT.name: John George II, Prince of Anhalt-Dessau
JOHANNGEORG2ANHALT.summary: Prince of Anhalt-Dessau from 1660 to 1693, of the family of Ascania. Married to Henrietta Catherine of Orange-Nassau, he was the father of Henryta Amalia and Leopold I.

ALEX4IMER.name: Alexander IV of Imereti
ALEX4IMER.summary: Son of Bagrat V, returned to the throne with Ottoman support and faced the factions that favoured Archil. His two reigns ended in new expulsions; his death did not end the rivalry between the two lines.

COSIMO2TOSC.name: Cosimo II of Tuscany
COSIMO2TOSC.summary: Grand Duke of Tuscany between 1609 and 1621. He protected Galileo Galilei, who in 1610 baptized in his honor the moons of Jupiter as "Medicean stars."

ANDRO3PALA.name: Andronikos III Palaiologos
ANDRO3PALA.summary: Byzantine Emperor since 1328 after a civil war against his grandfather Andronikos II. He lost almost all of Asia Minor to the Ottomans, but he recovered Tesalia and the Epirus.

JEANNEPENTHIEVRE.name: Joan of Penthièvre
JEANNEPENTHIEVRE.summary: A daughter of Guy of Brittany and niece of John III, she claimed the duchy against John of Montfort. Her husband, Charles of Blois, defended her cause by force of arms.
JEANNEPENTHIEVRE.biography: A daughter of Guy of Brittany and niece of John III, she claimed the duchy against John of Montfort. Her husband, Charles of Blois, defended her cause by force of arms. After her party’s defeat and Charles’s death, the Treaty of Guérande recognised the Montfort line in the duchy, while she retained her hereditary position in Penthièvre.

ALEX3IMER.name: Alexander III of Imereti
ALEX3IMER.summary: He sought to strengthen the crown in front of the Dadiani and took advantage of Mingrelia's succession changes to expand its influence. His marriage to Darejan, daughter of Teimuraz I, linked Imereti to the Kakheti branch.

MANFREDOATENAS.name: Manfred of Athens
MANFREDOATENAS.summary: Son of Frederick II of Sicily and Leonor of Anjou. In 1312 the Catalan Company, owner of Athens since the battle of Cefiso, asked the king for a son as Duke, and Frederick appointed Manfredo, still a child. He never left Sicily: the duchy was ruled by vicars-general. He died in Trapani in 1317 when he fell from the horse.

governmentNotes.Primer duque catalán, nombrado niño a pe: First Catalan Duke, appointed child at the request of the Company. He did not leave Sicily: vicars-general were ruled.

FELIPAHENAO.name: Philippa of Hainaut
FELIPAHENAO.summary: Consort of the Avesnes dynasty. Their life was connected with England and Hainaut.

MAGNUS1SAJLAU.name: Magnus I of Saxe-Lauenburg
MAGNUS1SAJLAU.summary: Duke of Saxony-Lauenburg from 1507 to 1543, of the family of Ascania. His daughters Dorotea and Catalina married Cristian III of Denmark and Gustavo I of Sweden.

JUANBORJAENR.name: Juan de Borja y Enríquez de Luna
JUANBORJAENR.summary: Duke of Gandía, 1497–1543. Duke of the Borgia dynasty.

HENRY1CYPRUS.name: Henry I of Cyprus
HENRY1CYPRUS.summary: He acceded to the throne as a child and his minority triggered the struggle between the Ibelin and Frederick II. The resistance to imperial intervention consolidated a Cypriot monarchy with a nobility capable of conditioning the government.

ELEONORMAGNEU.name: Eleanor Magdalena of Palatinate-Neuburg
ELEONORMAGNEU.summary: Consort of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Their life was connected with Holy Roman Empire and Palatinate.

CRISTINASAJDIN.name: Christina of Saxony
CRISTINASAJDIN.summary: Wife of King John and daughter of the house of Wettin. She defended Stockholm during the Swedish rebellion of 1501 and was held prisoner after capitulation. She was the mother of Christian II: her experience illustrates the fragility of the common government before the last attempt to preserve the union.

EMANUELFILIBERTOCAR.name: Emmanuel Philibert Amadeus of Savoy-Carignano
EMANUELFILIBERTOCAR.summary: A son of Thomas Francis and Marie of Bourbon-Soissons, he continued the Carignano branch. His marriage to Angela Caterina d’Este added an Italian connection to his Savoyard and Bourbon inheritance.
EMANUELFILIBERTOCAR.biography: A son of Thomas Francis and Marie of Bourbon-Soissons, he continued the Carignano branch. His marriage to Angela Caterina d’Este added an Italian connection to his Savoyard and Bourbon inheritance. The line descending from his son Victor Amadeus traces the generations between the branch’s founders and the future King Charles Albert.

JOHNREGENTCYP.name: John of Lusignan, Regent of Cyprus
aliases: John of Lusignan, Prince of Antioch
JOHNREGENTCYP.summary: Brother of Peter I, he ruled during the minority of Peter II. The charges and revenge that followed the king's murder faced the members of the court. His title as Prince of Antioch was nominal, for the principality had disappeared.

CRISTINASAXHESSE.name: Christina of Saxony
CRISTINASAXHESSE.summary: Consort of the Wettin dynasty. Their life was connected with Saxony and Hesse.

ISAB1B.name: Elizabeth of Bohemia
ISAB1B.summary: Consort of the Přemyslid dynasty. Their life was connected with Bohemia.

FERN3TOSC.name: Ferdinand III of Tuscany
FERN3TOSC.summary: Grand Duke of Tuscany, 1790–1799. Grand duke of the Habsburg-Lorraine dynasty.

governmentNotes.Gobierno efectivo hasta la salida de mar: Effective government until March 1799. The 1799 / 1800 versions do not maintain that geometry as a uniform effective domain.

ISABELINGHOH.name: Isabella of England
ISABELINGHOH.summary: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their life was connected with Holy Roman Empire and England.

MARIAMANUELA.name: Maria Manuela of Portugal
MARIAMANUELA.summary: Consort of the Aviz dynasty. Their life was connected with Spain.

AMEDEO6SAB.name: Amadeus VI of Savoy
AMEDEO6SAB.summary: Known as the Green Count, he belonged to the generation that strengthened Savoy’s political and military reach. He was the son of Aymon and Yolanda of Montferrat, bringing together Savoyard and Palaiologan ancestry.
AMEDEO6SAB.biography: Known as the Green Count, he belonged to the generation that strengthened Savoy’s political and military reach. He was the son of Aymon and Yolanda of Montferrat, bringing together Savoyard and Palaiologan ancestry. His marriage to Bonne of Bourbon added a French connection to a family already linked with Milan and Byzantium.

TAMARKARTLI.name: Tamar of Kartli
TAMARKARTLI.summary: A daughter of Vakhtang VI and wife of Teimuraz II, she linked the branches of Kartli and Kakheti. She was the mother of Heraclius II, who united both crowns in 1762.

MARGARTOIS.name: Margaret of Artois
MARGARTOIS.summary: Consort of the Artois dynasty. Their life was connected with France.

LUISAULRICAPRUSIA.name: Louisa Ulrika of Prussia
LUISAULRICAPRUSIA.summary: Consort of the Hohenzollern dynasty. Their life was connected with Prussia and Sweden.

ELEONOREMARIAAUT.name: Eleonore Maria Josefa of Austria
ELEONOREMARIAAUT.summary: Archduchess of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life was connected with Austria and Lorraine.

IVAN3MOSC.name: Ivan III of Moscow
IVAN3MOSC.summary: Grand Prince of Russia, 1462–1505. Grand prince of the Rurikid dynasty.

HELENAEREKLE.name: Helena of Kartli-Kakheti
HELENAEREKLE.summary: Daughter of Heraclius II and wife of Prince Archil of Imereti. She was the mother of Solomon II: this connection helps explain the eastern support for his candidacy to the Western throne.

FADRIQUEALVAREZ.name: Fadrique Álvarez de Toledo y Enríquez
FADRIQUEALVAREZ.summary: Duke of the Álvarez de Toledo dynasty. Their life was connected with Castile.

SILKENTHOMAS.name: Thomas FitzGerald, X Count of Kildare
SILKENTHOMAS.summary: He led the rebellion in 1534 after receiving news about his father's fate. The defeat and its execution in London ended with the immediate hegemony of the Kildare. The subsequent restoration of his half-brother preserved the continuity of the lineage.

GEORGESAX.name: George of Saxony
GEORGESAX.summary: George the Bearded, Duke of the Saxony albertine since 1500 and defender of Catholicism in front of Luther. He organized the Leipzig dispute of 1519 between Luther and Johann Eck.

MARGMONFERRATO.name: Margaret of Montferrat
MARGMONFERRATO.summary: Consort of the Paleologa-Monferrato dynasty. Their life was connected with Montferrat and Urgel.

ALF2PROVENZA.name: Alfonso II of Provence
ALF2PROVENZA.summary: The son of Alfonso II of Aragon, he ruled Provence in the name of his father since 1185 and remained count until his death in 1196. In 1193 he married Garsenda of Sabran, a heiress of Forcalquier, a county that thus joined Provence. He died in 1209; his son Ramón Berenguer succeeded him.

governmentNotes.Gobernó el condado en nombre de su padre: He ruled the county on behalf of his father.
governmentNotes.Por su matrimonio con Garsenda de Sabran: For his marriage to Garsenda of Sabran (1193) he joined Forcalquier to Provence.

LUDOVICO1SAL.name: Ludovico I of Saluzzo
LUDOVICO1SAL.summary: He inherited as a child, under a regency in which his half-brother Valerano played a prominent role. His long rule kept Saluzzo between Savoyard pressure and French protection.
LUDOVICO1SAL.biography: He inherited as a child, under a regency in which his half-brother Valerano played a prominent role. His long rule kept Saluzzo between Savoyard pressure and French protection. He married Isabella of Montferrat; their son was Ludovico II. Feudal dependence and agreements with neighbouring powers did not extinguish the marquisate’s own institutions.

JOVANBRANK.name: Jovan Branković
JOVANBRANK.summary: The son of Stefan and Angelina, he initially shared the dignity of despot with his brother Đorđe. The title was held in the Hungarian political sphere and did not entail the recovery of Serbia. His daughter Elena married Petru Rareș, so the descendants of the Branković linked with the Moldovan court.

governmentNotes.Título nominal, compartido inicialmente: Nominal title, initially shared with his brother Đorđe; Serbia was under Ottoman rule.

MARIAANABAV1660.name: Maria Anna Victoria of Bavaria
MARIAANABAV1660.summary: Consort of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Their life was connected with France and Bavaria.

FEDERICORANDAZZO.name: Frederick I of Athens
FEDERICORANDAZZO.role: Marquis of Randazzo · Duke of Athens and Neopatras
FEDERICORANDAZZO.summary: A son of John of Randazzo, he inherited the duchies of Athens and Neopatras in 1348. At his death in 1355, they passed to his cousin, King Frederick III of Sicily.

governmentNotes.A su muerte los ducados pasaron a su pri: At his death the duchies passed to his cousin Frederick III of Sicily.

ALEXIS1RUS.name: Alexis of Russia
ALEXIS1RUS.summary: Tsar of Russia, 1645–1676. Tsar of the Romanov dynasty.

JEANTARTAS.name: John of Albret, Viscount of Tartas
JEANTARTAS.summary: A son of Charles II of Albret and father of Alain, he died before his own father. He therefore occupies an intermediate generation in the genealogy without appearing as an equivalent link in the succession to the lordship. This distinction explains how a grandson could inherit directly from his grandfather.

ERIK2NORWAY.name: Erik II from Norway
ERIK2NORWAY.summary: A son of Magnus VI and Ingeborg of Denmark, his marriage to Margaret of Scotland made him the father of the Norwegian Maid, the Scottish heiress who died before reaching her kingdom. When Erik died without a surviving son, his brother Haakon V succeeded him.

TEODORO2MON.name: Theodore II of Montferrat
TEODORO2MON.summary: A son of John II and Isabella of Majorca, he inherited Montferrat after his brother John III. His rule was shaped by relations with Milan and disputes with Savoy-Achaea.
TEODORO2MON.biography: A son of John II and Isabella of Majorca, he inherited Montferrat after his brother John III. His rule was shaped by relations with Milan and disputes with Savoy-Achaea. His son John James succeeded him. His ancestry preserves the Majorcan connection of the Italian Palaiologoi.

ALEXANDER1RUS.name: Alexander I of Russia
ALEXANDER1RUS.summary: Emperor of Russia since 1801. Faced with Napoleon, he resisted the invasion of 1812 and played a central role in the Congress of Vienna and the Holy Alliance.

GIANGIORGIOMON.name: Gian Giorgio of Montferrat
GIANGIORGIOMON.summary: A son of Boniface III and brother of William IX, he succeeded his nephew Boniface IV. He was the last marquis of the legitimate male Palaiologos line.
GIANGIORGIOMON.biography: A son of Boniface III and brother of William IX, he succeeded his nephew Boniface IV. He was the last marquis of the legitimate male Palaiologos line. His death in 1533 opened a dispute over Montferrat; the later imperial settlement in favour of the Gonzaga rested on the rights of his niece Margaret.

HELENAPALACYP.name: Helena Palaiologina
HELENAPALACYP.summary: A daughter of Theodore II of Morea and wife of John II of Cyprus, she favoured the island’s Greek institutions. She was the mother of Charlotte. Her presence at court illustrates the links between the Lusignan Mediterranean and the last Byzantine world.

WILLIAM2ORANGE.name: William II of Orange
WILLIAM2ORANGE.summary: Stadtholder of Low Countries, 1647–1650 (Delegated government). Prince of Orange of the Nassau dynasty.

governmentNotes.Cargo provincial delegado por los Estado: Provincial position delegated by the States, with documented personal fields and dates; not hereditary sovereignty over the whole Republic or the Spanish provinces.

CAROLINEANSB.name: Caroline of Ansbach
CAROLINEANSB.summary: Consort of the Hohenzollern dynasty. Their life was connected with Brandenburg and England.

ANNASOPHIEDENSAX.name: Anna Sophia of Denmark
ANNASOPHIEDENSAX.summary: Consort of the Oldenburg dynasty. Their life was connected with Denmark and Saxony.

JOACHIMFREDBRAND.name: Joachim Frederick of Brandenburg
JOACHIMFREDBRAND.summary: Brandenburg Elector between 1598 and 1608. In 1605 he assumed the administration of the duchy of Prussia for the disease of his Duke, a step before the union of both territories.

ANNASAXALBERT.name: Anna of Saxony
ANNASAXALBERT.summary: Consort of the Wettin dynasty. Their life was connected with Saxony and Brandenburg.

ELISADENBRAND.name: Elizabeth of Denmark
ELISADENBRAND.summary: Consort of the Oldenburg dynasty. Their life was connected with Denmark and Brandenburg.

KESTUTISLIT.name: Kęstutis
KESTUTISLIT.summary: Prince of Trakai and chief of the Western defence under Algirdas. He briefly removed Jogaila and was a great duke in 1381-1382. He died captive in Kreva; he was the father of Vitauts the Great.

governmentNotes.Gobierno patrimonial occidental y superi: Western inheritance government and superiority over Samogitia, other than the title of great duke.
governmentNotes.Desde finales de 1381 hasta mediados de: From the end of 1381 to the mid-1382; the annual map conserves the conflict with Jogaila.

BLANCANAMUR.name: Blanche of Namur
BLANCANAMUR.summary: A daughter of the comital house of Namur and wife of Magnus Eriksson. Their sons Erik and Haakon took part in the divisions of power in Sweden and Norway.
BLANCANAMUR.biography: A daughter of the comital house of Namur and wife of Magnus Eriksson. Their sons Erik and Haakon took part in the divisions of power in Sweden and Norway. The marriage connected the Nordic monarchy with noble networks in the Low Countries, without transferring any territory from Namur to Scandinavia.

WEN1.name: Wenceslaus I of Bohemia
WEN1.summary: It consolidated the Přemysl monarchy in Bohemia and favored the growth of cities and internal colonization. His reign coincided with the Mongolian invasion of Central Europe.

LEONORARAGCAST.name: Eleanor of Aragon
LEONORARAGCAST.summary: Consort of the Barcelona dynasty. Their life was connected with Castile and Aragon.

FRED1SAX.name: Frederick I of Saxony
FRED1SAX.summary: Margrave of Meissen who in 1423 received from the Emperor Segismundo the Duchy and Elected of Saxony, starting the Wettin government in the electorate.

GASTONNEMOURS.name: Gaston of Foix, Duke of Nemours
GASTONNEMOURS.summary: The son of John of Foix and Mary of Orleans, he was nephew of Louis XII and brother of Germana of Foix. He led French forces during the wars in Italy and died in the battle of Ravenna in 1512. His career brings together the Pirenaic connections of the Foix and military service to the French monarchy.

GEDIMINASLIT.name: Gedimas
GEDIMINASLIT.summary: Great duke and central figure of the gedimida dynasty. His letters invited Western merchants and craftsmen; Vilna was consolidated as capital and family alliances expanded Lithuanian influence on the ruthenian lands.

ARNAUROGER2PALLARS.name: Arnau Roger II of Pallars
ARNAUROGER2PALLARS.summary: The son of Hugh de Matapala and Countess Sibila, shared the county with her mother until 1330 and ruled until 1343. He died without children, and Peter IV granted Pallars to his brother Ramón Roger.

governmentNotes.Compartió el gobierno con su madre hasta: He shared the government with his mother until 1330.
